g.text: The LKT augmented GRU: predict first, then update memory
Forward-only: 3 GRU layers × 32 units | 21 predictor coordinates | 20,977 parameter entries
A Network at one trial t, for one participant
1 Predict from inputs and PREVIOUS memory
Previous TOP-layer memory goes to the head
Retain ALL three states for the next trial: [h1(t), h2(t), h3(t)] = 3 × 32 values
Each new participant starts with zero states. New memory h3(t) can affect the NEXT prediction, p(t+1).
Dropout locations are shown for training; dropout is disabled during evaluation and continuation.
B Inside one GRU layer: the exact Torch reset/update equations
Every layer has separate weights and biases. u(t) has 22 coordinates in layer 1 and 32 in layers 2 and 3.
for g in {reset r, update z, new n}
Each a_g and c_g has 32 values
⊙ means elementwise multiplication. The reset gate multiplies c_n INCLUDING its recurrent bias, as in torch::nn_gru.
LKT columns: intercept, student logitdec, KC PPES, and student–KC logitdec. The centered intercept coordinate is zero.
Training also compares p(t) with y(t) using binary cross-entropy. Continuation updates hidden states while weights stay fixed.
Reported probabilities are clipped to [ε, 1−ε], with ε = 10⁻⁵. Training loss uses the un-clipped logits.
Source: R/lkt-model-gru.R and R/lkt-gru-prediction.R. Dimensions and equations verified against augmented_g003_seed1.
